findings.finding: Gulf of America volumes printed only 110 Mboed in Q3 (against full quarters usually 130+ Mboed), cut by a September curtailment from a third-party gas pipeline constraint and maintenance that the company said was only 'partially restored' on 13 Oct. Hurricane Isaias then forced ~72% of Gulf oil (about 1.5m b/d) to shut in around 7-12 Oct. Both point to a Q4 Gulf production guide below a normal quarter when OXY guides on 9 Nov.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (5 Aug): production beat the guide midpoint by 23 Mboed and full-year guidance was raised; the stock rose +4.14% the next session. Q1 2026 (5 May): -7.11% on a revenue miss as oil fell. Production and guidance have mattered on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Both facts are public. What is not public is how OXY quantifies the Q4 Gulf hit and whether the third-party pipeline is fully back. If the market had priced a soft Q4 guide, consensus would carry a visibly lower Q4 production number. No source I found shows Q4 revisions, and the stock's 13% fall last week tracks the oil move, not production.
findings.independence: Hurricane shut-in from Reuters via BOE Report, 2026-10-09 (https://boereport.com/2026/10/09/us-gulf-producers-shut-in-more-oil-and-gas-as-isaias-nears-landfall/). It does not name OXY, so OXY's own exposure to the storm is inferred. Different document from the 8-K.

findings.finding: Sequential arithmetic from pre-released numbers suggests consensus of $1.43 is low. Realized oil fell from $96.78 to $85.91/bbl (about -$0.86B pre-tax on ~690 Mb/d). Domestic gas rose from -$1.48 to +$1.61/Mcf (about +$0.45B on ~1.6 Bcf/d). Collar losses fell from $156m to $94m (+$62m). LOE rose about $0.74/boe (-$80m). That is upstream about -$0.4B pre-tax. Going from Q2's $2.40 to $1.43 then needs midstream to fall from $961m to roughly $150-250m. A midstream figure near $350m (Waha spread narrowed but not gone, record sulfur) implies roughly $1.55-1.65, close to the $1.60 whisper.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: EPS beat with midstream at more than double its guide midpoint; stock +4.14% next session. Q1 2026: miss, -7.11%.
findings.why_not_priced: Management gave no Q3 midstream dollar number, only 'expect third quarter income to decline as the Waha to Gulf Coast spread narrows', so the street's midstream estimate is a guess. The $0.17 gap between whisper ($1.60) and consensus ($1.43) shows part of the market already expects this. It is inference, and the volume and tax assumptions are mine, not the company's.
findings.independence: Shares inputs with the 13 Oct 8-K (https://last10k.com/sec-filings/oxy/0001628280-26-065586.htm). The Waha recovery to $1.50-2/MMBtu since July (RBN, via search) and the whisper (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/OXY) point the same way. Not a company number.

findings.finding: Peers that reported after OXY's 13 Oct pre-release beat consensus on the same oil tape. Diamondback adjusted EPS was $5.86 against $5.46 LSEG and $4.92 Zacks, with realized oil $87.30 against OXY's $85.91. ConocoPhillips was $3.27 against $3.06 Zacks. EOG revenue was $5.85B against $5.59B. That suggests sell-side oil-name estimates lagged the Q3 price mix.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: OXY rose +4.14% on its Q2 beat. I found no sourced price reaction for the peers' Q3 2026 beats, so this beat pattern has no measured reaction attached.
findings.why_not_priced: OXY's consensus at $1.43 sits well below the $1.60 whisper, so the published bar has not caught up with the peer beats. If it had, aggregator consensus would have moved toward $1.55-1.60 in the week since the peers reported. A beat may still be swamped by the oil tape.
findings.independence: COP and EOG Q3 2026 from a different outlet (oilprice.com / Zacks via search: https://oilprice.com/Company-News/EOG-Resources-Lifts-Dividend-8-as-Q3-Profit-Surges-89.html). Proxy for OXY, not OXY's own number.

findings.finding: Pre-released Q3 domestic LOE was $8.54/boe against the company's own Q3 guide of $8.75. Crude collar settlements cost $94m, against $156m in Q2. Both are small favourable items inside or below guidance.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not separable in past reactions; the cost line has not been what OXY trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: pre-released four weeks ago. About $0.21/boe on ~1.15 MMboe/d domestic is ~$22m pre-tax, or ~$0.02/share.
findings.independence: Q3 LOE guide of $8.75 is from the Q2 call transcript (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/OXY/Q22026); same company, different document.

findings.finding: OXY fell ~13% into the print, from ~$64 on 2 Nov to ~$55.80 on 9 Nov, as WTI dropped ~15% in a week to ~$86 on hopes after the midterms that the Iran war would end. Retail sentiment fell to 21% bullish. The Q4 and 2027 guide will be read against an oil price the stock has already marked down, so the bar for the forward commentary is lower than a week ago.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026: -7.11% on the print as oil retreated sharply, so oil direction over the window has dominated before.
findings.why_not_priced: The oil fall is priced by definition. The range is wide because WTI's move on 10 Nov, unpredictable, will likely matter more than the print. Filed so the judges see that oil beta dominates this window.
findings.independence: Price levels from Fox Business quote pages (https://www.foxbusiness.com/quote?stockTicker=OXY) and the EW preview (https://finviz.com/news/413849/occidentals-midstream-windfall-fades-as-deleveraging-story-faces-its-first-real-test).

findings.finding: Principal debt was $11.8B after Q2 against a $10.0B milestone, with Q2 free cash flow of $3.0B before working capital. A Q3 at $86 oil could bring debt close to the milestone. But management said buybacks stay 'opportunistic' and a continuous program is a lower priority until the August 2029 preferred redemption, and that it would 'lean towards more principal debt reduction'. Devon, by contrast, guided to more than $1B of Q4 buybacks.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced reaction to a capital-return change on this name in 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: Whether OXY reports reaching or nearing $10B, and what it says follows, is unknown until the release and the 10 Nov call. If the market expected buybacks, the peer contrast (Devon) would not stand out. Management's own words cap the upside, hence the small size.
findings.independence: Devon buyback guidance (https://oilprice.com/Company-News/Devon-Energy-Posts-2-Billion-in-Free-Cash-Flow-as-Buybacks-Accelerate.html). The Q2 release confirms $11.8B debt and $3.0B FCF (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000797468/000162828026053377/oxyex9916-30x26earningsrel.htm).

findings.finding: The 2027 framework is due on this call. On the Q2 call management gave a $5.9B starting point for 2027 capex and roughly $5.0-5.1B of sustaining capital. Any number above $5.9B, or higher activity at ~$86 oil, is a guidance swing either way.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: the $4B-by-2030 cash-flow plan came with a +4.14% reaction. No sourced history for a next-year capex framework.
findings.why_not_priced: The direction is not knowable from public documents. It is filed so the judges see the line the reaction may turn on; I gave it no size.
findings.independence: Same transcript as the capital-return finding; counts once.

findings.finding: Sulfur was at record prices through Q3: Tampa Q3 contract $705/lt, up $50 q/q, and Gulf FOB $1,100-1,150/t in July, because Middle East exports through Hormuz collapsed. That supports Al Hosn's sulfur economics in midstream, but OXY flagged 'sulfur logistics at Alhosn' as a constraint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Management flagged sulfur prices as a source of midstream volatility on the Q2 call; no separable reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: It is an industry proxy, and the logistics caveat cuts against it, hence a small size. If the street had modelled it, the Q3 midstream estimate would sit higher, and the whisper-consensus gap hints that some have.
findings.independence: CRU 2026 note on Middle East conflict pushing sulfur to new highs (https://www.crugroup.com/en/communities/thought-leadership/2026/middle-east-conflict-pushes-sulphur-and-acid-prices-to-new-heights/). Proxy only.
